issues.description: The tensor-network zero-state initializer is named differently across artifacts: the problem statement and the reference solution expect a function named create_zero_state(num_qubits), but the template repository defines init_zero_state(num_qubits). This mismatch (name create_zero_state vs init_zero_state) means tests and instructor-provided calls to create_zero_state will fail to find the student implementation and students following the task text will not see the expected symbol in the starter code, causing import/test failures and unnecessary confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template and problem statement consistent. Rename the template function init_zero_state to create_zero_state (preserving the same signature), or add a one-line wrapper in the template: def create_zero_state(num_qubits): return init_zero_state(num_qubits). Update the header/task text if needed so all three artifacts (problem statement, template, tests/solution) reference the same function name.
